methodology: One row per real-world crash, not per article. Media, operator, regulator and research references describing the same event are merged into a canonical incident record. A match requires a compatible event date, location and vehicle/operator; ambiguous reports remain separate until verified.
limitations: This is a discovery-based tracker, not an exhaustive census. Unlike the U.S. NHTSA SGO, the EU does not currently publish a centralized incident-level ADS crash feed. Coverage depends on public reporting and may miss unreported incidents.

incidents.narrative: A Navya autonomous shuttle operating in Vienna's Seestadt pilot collided with a 30-year-old pedestrian at low speed. Wiener Linien said witnesses reported that the pedestrian, wearing headphones and looking at a phone, crossed into the side of the bus. The pedestrian was treated for minor scratches and the pilot was temporarily suspended while logs were reviewed.

incidents.automation: Automated bus trial; safety driver onboard
incidents.narrative: On the first day carrying passengers, an autonomous e-ATAK bus braked and was struck from behind by a tram in Gothenburg. A small number of passengers were onboard. Västtrafik reported no casualties or personal injuries; both vehicles sustained damage and the bus was removed from service for inspection.

reporting_options.scope: EU/EEA fully automated vehicles covered by the type-approval framework
reporting_options.access: Reported to authorities; no public incident-level feed identified
reporting_options.notes: Manufacturers must notify safety-critical occurrences and provide short-term and annual in-service occurrence reporting to type-approval/market-surveillance authorities and the European Commission.

reporting_options.scope: EU road crashes involving death or injury
reporting_options.access: European Commission road-safety database; detailed national crash records
reporting_options.notes: Potential backstop for injury/fatal crashes, but the standard public CARE description does not identify ADS engagement, so matching would require country/date/location/vehicle information.

reporting_options.source: National crash databases and transport authorities
reporting_options.scope: Member-state police/hospital crash records and AV trial permits
reporting_options.access: Varies by country; some datasets require access requests
reporting_options.notes: Example: Sweden's STRADA combines police and hospital injury-crash information. National transport/type-approval agencies may also hold ADS occurrence reports that are not centrally published.
Current beta source. Multiple articles about one crash are merged into one canonical incident. Operator and public-agency statements are preferred when available.
